benefits_en:
1. An accepted Hajj (Hajj Mabrur) has no reward except Paradise.
2. One Umrah to the next serves as expiation for whatever minor sins occur between them.

1. Whoever performs Hajj for Allah's sake without indulging in obscenity or transgression returns pure from sins like the day their mother gave birth to them.
2. Complete spiritual rebirth through sincere pilgrimage.

1. Follow up between Hajj and Umrah continuously, for they eliminate poverty and sins just as the furnace purges dross from iron, gold, and silver.
2. Spiritual and material prosperity fostered through regular pilgrimage.

1. Performing Umrah during the blessed month of Ramadan is equivalent in reward to performing Hajj with the Prophet ﷺ.
2. Multiplied honor and merit of righteous deeds in sacred times.

1. 'Hajj is 'Arafah': standing in supplication and repentance at the plains of 'Arafah on the 9th of Dhul-Hijjah is the indispensable pillar of Hajj.
2. Fulfilling the core rite of 'Arafah secures the validity of the pilgrimage.

1. There is no day on which Allah frees more servants from the Fire than the Day of 'Arafah.
2. Allah draws near and boasts of the gathered pilgrims to the angels in the highest heavens.

1. The Prophet's ﷺ definitive instruction during the Farewell Pilgrimage: 'Learn your pilgrimage rites from me.'
2. Adherence to strict prophetic practice in every rite of Hajj and Umrah.

1. The best supplication is the supplication on the Day of 'Arafah, and the best declaration is: 'La ilaha illallah wahdahu la sharika lahu...'
2. Tawhid is the supreme core of all pilgrimage supplications.

1. The Black Stone (Al-Hajar al-Aswad) and Yemeni Corner expiate sins; touching or kissing them is an act of pure devotion and obedience.
2. Following the Sunnah with reverence for sacred landmarks.

1. Circumambulating the Ka'bah (Tawaf) is like prayer, except that speech is permitted during it; therefore speak only what is good.
2. Preserving modesty, mindfulness, and reverence during Tawaf.

1. The water of Zamzam is blessed for whatever purpose it is drunk with sincere intention.
2. Nourishing physical healing and spiritual fulfillment from this blessed well.

1. The Sa'i between Safa and Marwah commemorates the reliance and devotion of Lady Hajar (AS).
2. Cultivating unwavering trust in Allah's provision amidst life's struggles.

1. The Prophet ﷺ prayed three times for forgiveness for those who shave their heads (Halq) after pilgrimage, and once for those who trim (Taqsir).
2. Shaving represents total surrender and humility before the Creator.

1. One prayer in the Sacred Mosque (Al-Masjid al-Haram in Makkah) is superior to one hundred thousand prayers elsewhere.
2. One prayer in the Prophet's Mosque (Madinah) is superior to one thousand prayers elsewhere.

1. The area between my house and my pulpit is a Garden (Rawdah) from the gardens of Paradise.
2. Sacred sanctity and multiplied blessing of worship within the Prophet's Mosque.

1. Whoever purifies himself at home and comes to the Mosque of Quba' to pray two rak'ahs receives the reward of an Umrah.
2. The high virtue of visiting and praying in Masjid Quba'.

1. Prohibition of undertaking journeys specifically to seek blessing in mosques except for three: Al-Masjid al-Haram, Al-Masjid an-Nabawi, and Al-Masjid al-Aqsa.
2. Preserving the unique theological rank of the three holy sanctuaries.

1. The first ten days of Dhul-Hijjah are the most beloved days of the entire year to Allah for righteous deeds.
2. Intensifying fasting, dhikr, charity, and Qur'an recitation during these ten sacred days.

1. The sacrificial offering (Udhiyah/Qurbani) on Eid al-Adha and the days of Tashriq is the most beloved deed to Allah on that day.
2. Commemorating the sacrifice of Prophet Ibrahim (AS) and distributing meat to the poor.

1. The days of Tashriq (11th, 12th, and 13th of Dhul-Hijjah) are days of eating, drinking, and remembering Allah the Almighty.
2. Combining lawful worldly enjoyment with constant remembrance of Allah.

1. Whoever sets out on a path seeking sacred knowledge, Allah makes easy for them a path leading to Paradise.
2. Knowledge of the Qur'an and Sunnah is the ultimate road map to eternal salvation.

1. The angels lower their wings in humble approval and joy for the seeker of beneficial Islamic knowledge.
2. Cosmic reverence and heavenly honor bestowed upon sincere students of knowledge.

1. All creatures in the heavens and on earth, even the fish swimming in the depths of the oceans, ask forgiveness for the scholar.
2. The widespread blessing that beneficial scholarship brings to all creation.

1. The superiority of the scholar over the devout worshiper is like the brilliance of the full moon over all other stars.
2. Knowledge guides and validates worship, protecting from deviation.

1. The scholars are the true inheritors of the Prophets; prophets leave behind neither dinars nor dirhams, but knowledge.
2. Whoever acquires knowledge has taken an abundant, noble share of prophetic legacy.

1. When Allah desires supreme good for a person, He grants them deep understanding (Fiqh) of the religion.
2. Comprehension of divine revelation is the highest mark of divine favor.

1. Seeking knowledge is an obligatory duty upon every individual Muslim according to their daily religious needs.
2. Fulfilling the foundational knowledge of creed, prayer, halal, and haram.

1. 'Convey from me, even if it is a single verse': duty of every believer to share what they have authentically learned.
2. Encourages continuous propagation of truth with accuracy.

1. May Allah brighten with joy and honor the face of a person who hears my speech, understands it, memorizes it, and conveys it accurately.
2. Prophetic supplication for those who preserve and transmit the Sunnah.

1. Severe warning against intentionally fabricating lies or attributing false statements to the Prophet ﷺ; their seat is in Hellfire.
2. Absolute imperative of verifying hadith authenticity and referencing.

1. Severe warning against seeking religious knowledge for worldly prestige, disputing with scholars, or impressing people.
2. Purification of intention is the lifeblood of authentic scholarship.

1. Severe warning against concealing beneficial knowledge when asked; Allah will bridle the concealer with a bridle of fire on Judgment Day.
2. Obligation of sharing knowledge generously with seekers.

1. Knowledge is taken away not by pulling it out from people's chests, but through the death of upright scholars.
2. When ignorant leaders are consulted, they issue rulings without knowledge, straying and leading others astray.

1. Whoever guides someone to a good deed receives a reward equal to the one who performs it.
2. Immense multiplying power of Islamic teaching, mentorship, and Da'wah.

1. Whoever initiates a good Sunnah (beneficial practice rooted in Islam) earns its reward and the reward of all who practice it until the Day of Judgment.
2. Leading by example in establishing righteous habits and institutions.

1. Whoever calls people to misguidance carries the burden of their sin and the sins of all who follow them.
2. Terrifying danger of spreading falsehood, innovation, and vice.

1. No two traits are ever found together in a hypocrite: good conduct and deep understanding of the religion.
2. True knowledge necessarily manifests in moral refinement and righteous behavior.

1. The best of you in the Pre-Islamic days of ignorance (Jahiliyyah) are the best in Islam, provided they attain deep understanding of the religion.
2. Directing human talent and character through the purifying light of revelation.

1. Asking good questions is half of knowledge, and seeking clarification with humility is the hallmark of genuine students.
2. Cultivating respectful intellectual curiosity in learning.

1. The parable of divine guidance and knowledge is like abundant rain falling upon fertile ground that absorbs water and produces lush vegetation.
2. Hearts vary in their receptivity: some absorb and benefit, some preserve for others, and barren rocks gain nothing.

1. The feet of a servant will not move on Judgment Day until asked about four: their life and how spent, youth and how consumed, wealth and how earned and spent, and knowledge and how acted upon.
2. Accountability of translating knowledge into righteous practice.

1. Seeking refuge in Allah from four: knowledge that does not benefit, a heart that does not fear, a soul that is never satisfied, and a supplication that is not answered.
2. Aligning intellectual acquisition with spiritual humility and action.

1. Supplicating daily: 'Allahumma inni as'aluka 'ilman nafi'an, wa rizqan tayyiban, wa 'amalan mutaqabbalan' (O Allah, I ask You for beneficial knowledge, wholesome sustenance, and accepted deeds).
2. The ultimate triad for a blessed and purposeful daily life.

1. Sincere envy (Ghibtah/noble competition) is permissible in only two cases: a person given wealth who spends it entirely in truth, and a person given wisdom who judges by it and teaches it.
2. Channeling ambition toward benevolent generosity and scholarly teaching.

1. By Allah, that Allah guides a single person through you is vastly better for you than possessing the most valuable red camels.
2. Guiding a lost soul back to truth is the most precious achievement in human existence.

1. The Prophet's ﷺ methodology in teaching: making things easy and not difficult, giving glad tidings and not causing aversion.
2. Gentleness, encouragement, and wisdom in religious education.

1. Teaching with clarity and repetition: repeating important words three times so that listeners fully comprehend.
2. Ensuring complete pedagogical clarity and comprehension for all students.

1. Patience in teaching: the Prophet ﷺ never rebuked or humiliated a learner who made an error out of ignorance.
2. Compassion and constructive correction in mentorship.

1. Writing down knowledge to preserve it: 'Tie down knowledge by writing.'
2. Documenting, recording, and cataloging Islamic knowledge for future generations.

1. Whoever is asked about knowledge and says 'I do not know' has demonstrated true scholarly integrity and wisdom.
2. Humility in acknowledging intellectual limits protects the religion from false conjecture.

1. The best of you are those who learn the Qur'an and teach it to others.
2. Dedicating one's life to the study and dissemination of Allah's revelation earns the highest status in this Ummah.

1. The one who is skilled in reciting the Qur'an will be in the company of the noble, righteous angel-scribes.
2. The one who stammers and struggles with difficulty receives a doubled reward for their persistent effort.

1. Read the Qur'an, for it will come on the Day of Resurrection as an intercessor for its regular companions.
2. The Qur'an acts as an eloquent advocate shielding its reciters from punishment.

1. The two luminous chapters, Surah al-Baqarah and Surah Al 'Imran, will appear on Judgment Day like two clouds or flocks of birds shading their reciter.
2. Protection and heavenly defense earned through mastering these two supreme chapters.

1. Satan flees from any house in which Surah al-Baqarah is recited.
2. Sanctifying the domestic home and expelling negative spiritual forces through Qur'anic recitation.

1. Ayat al-Kursi (the Verse of the Throne, al-Baqarah: 255) is the greatest single verse in the entire Book of Allah.
2. Comprehensive exposition of Allah's sovereign majesty, life, knowledge, and power.

1. Whoever recites Ayat al-Kursi after every obligatory prayer, nothing stands between them and entering Paradise except death.
2. Firm preservation of this daily post-prayer protective fortress.

1. Whoever recites the last two verses of Surah al-Baqarah at night, they will suffice him against all harm.
2. Nightly spiritual shielding through these sublime prophetic verses.

1. Surah al-Ikhlas (Say: He is Allah, the One) is equivalent to one-third of the entire Qur'an in theological value.
2. Pure affirmation of Tawhid and negation of all deficiency from the Creator.

1. Reciting Surah al-Ikhlas, Surah al-Falaq, and Surah an-Nas three times in the morning and evening protects against all forms of evil.
2. The comprehensive prophetic shielding against physical and spiritual harm.

1. Whoever memorizes the first ten verses of Surah al-Kahf is granted divine protection against the deception of the False Messiah (Dajjal).
2. Fortifying one's faith against end-times ideological tribulations.

1. Surah al-Mulk (Chapter 67) consists of thirty verses that persistently interceded for a man until his sins were completely forgiven.
2. Nightly recitation of Surah al-Mulk saves one from the torment of the grave.

1. Whoever recites a single letter from the Book of Allah receives a good deed, and that good deed is multiplied tenfold.
2. Immense multiplied spiritual wealth earned with every sentence of Qur'anic recitation.

1. It will be said to the companion of the Qur'an: 'Recite, ascend, and chant as you used to chant in the worldly life; your station is at the last verse you recite.'
2. Eternal elevation in Paradise proportional to one's memorization and devotion to the Qur'an.

1. Regularly review and maintain the Qur'an, for by the One in Whose Hand is my soul, it slips away faster than tied camels.
2. Discipline in daily revision (Muraja'ah) for memorizers of revelation.

1. A house in which the Qur'an is recited becomes spacious for its inhabitants, angels attend it, devils abandon it, and its blessings multiply.
2. The home devoid of Qur'an feels constricted and barren.

1. Indeed, Allah elevates by this Book some peoples and debases others.
2. Nations that uphold the Qur'an achieve honor and leadership; those that abandon it decline.

1. The people of the Qur'an are the chosen people of Allah and His closest inner circle among mankind.
2. Cherished proximity to the Divine through love of His sacred speech.

1. Beautify your voices with the Qur'an, for a melodious voice enhances the beauty and impact of the Qur'an.
2. Reciting with reverent rhythm and heartfelt emotion (Tartil).

1. The example of the believer who recites the Qur'an is like a fragrant citron, smelling delightful and tasting delicious.
2. The believer who does not recite is like a date, sweet in taste but without fragrance.

1. Allah does not listen to anything as attentatively as He listens to a Prophet reciting the Qur'an aloud with a sweet, melodious voice.
2. The sublime delight Allah takes in the sincere, heartfelt recitation of His Word.

1. Reflecting and weeping during Qur'anic recitation is the mark of true prophets and righteous saints.
2. Connecting the heart deeply with the warnings, promises, and parables of revelation.

1. No group gathers in one of the houses of Allah reciting the Book of Allah and studying it together, except that tranquility descends upon them, mercy envelops them, angels surround them, and Allah mentions them to those with Him.
2. Unmatched heavenly grace bestowed upon Qur'anic study circles (Halaqat).

1. The parents of the one who memorizes and lives by the Qur'an will be crowned on Judgment Day with a crown of light whose brilliance outshines the sun.
2. Immense honor bestowed upon parents who raise their children upon the Qur'an.

1. The Qur'an will come on the Day of Resurrection as a decisive argument either in your favor or against you.
2. Living by the Qur'an brings salvation; neglecting its commands brings condemnation.
